candidate_071.name: objective-separated discovery-vs-generalization acquisition lanes with Pareto audit
candidate_071.mechanism_hypothesis: A scientific acquisition loop should keep discovery yield and global predictive/generalization quality as separate objectives and observables rather than collapsing them into one generic acquisition score. Maintain distinct exploit/discovery and coverage/model-learning lanes, track a Pareto surface, and allow a higher-level controller to allocate budget according to the declared scientific objective and current marginal value. Promotion/generalization claims should be judged on leakage-controlled group-disjoint or prospective evidence that is not the same evidence used to optimize discovery yield.

primary_evidence.source: Krishna Harish, Objective-Dependent Active Learning and Calibrated Uncertainty for Sample-Efficient Discovery of Rare-Earth Extractants: A Benchmark on 1,202 Experimental Distribution Coefficients with Prospective Validation, ACS Omega 11(32):48692-48699, 2026, DOI 10.1021/acsomega.6c07482
primary_evidence.design: 1,202 experimental log D measurements covering 93 ligands, 14 lanthanides and 45 literature sources; active-learning comparisons use multiseed statistics (six seeds for the main acquisition figures), include both row-wise and chemically realistic ligand-batch acquisition, reproduce the core acquisition trade-off on an independent 4,200-compound log D benchmark, and finish with prospective testing on four independently synthesized ligands.
primary_evidence.main_result: At the row level, exploitation (greedy/UCB) reaches top-10 recall 1.00 but yields biased global models with R^2 about 0.63-0.70, whereas exploration/random yields the best predictive models at R^2 about 0.85-0.87 but row-level top-10 recall only 0.38-0.50. EI/hybrid lie on the Pareto front rather than dominating both objectives. Under a ligand-batch unit, exploitation still reaches top-10 ligand recall 1.00 versus 0.83 for random/exploration, while prediction is uniformly hard on a ligand-disjoint test and random is marginally best at R^2 0.30 versus 0.29 for exploitation.
primary_evidence.independent_benchmark: On 4,200 MoleculeNet Lipophilicity log D values with a different feature representation, exploration/random again give the best predictive models at R^2 about 0.50 but lowest design recall 0.20-0.27, while exploitation gives recall 0.53-0.57 but the worst predictive models at R^2 0.21-0.28.
primary_evidence.generalization_audit: A row-level random-forest estimate of R^2 0.94 collapses under leakage-controlled ligand/source/structural-family splits to roughly R^2 0.20 to -0.03. Prospective testing on four independently synthesized ligands yields R^2 0.70, RMSE 0.639 and MAE 0.502 log units, placing realistic transfer below the optimistic row-level estimate.
primary_evidence.objective_definition_boundary: The ranking also changes with what counts as a target: greedy row recall is 1.00 versus random 0.45, but at the unique-ligand level random reaches 0.95 versus greedy 0.82. Extraction strength and selectivity correlate only moderately (Spearman 0.63), with only 4 of the top 10 strongest extractants also in the top 10 most selective. Thus the acquisition objective and unit must be explicitly declared before comparing strategies.
primary_evidence.interpretation: This is direct science-domain evidence that discovery and model-learning/generalization are genuinely conflicting acquisition objectives and should remain separately observable. It materially strengthens the separate-lane part of candidate_069: a single fixed score or strategy can look optimal for one scientific objective while degrading another, and in-distribution performance can hide poor transfer.
primary_evidence.limits: The evidence supports objective separation and Pareto tracking, not the stronger claim that an autonomous higher-level controller can dynamically reallocate two lanes under support drift. The main domain is rare-earth extraction with one independent molecular benchmark; prospective validation uses four new ligands. The loop is pool-based rather than open-ended generative experiment design.

candidate_071.relation_to_existing: candidate_069 proposed objective-separated coverage/generalization and discovery lanes with drift-triggered reallocation, and candidate_070 supplied a narrower adaptive-vs-fixed diversity/uncertainty positive control. candidate_071 adds recent real-chemistry evidence that the two objectives themselves conflict under matched acquisition benchmarks and that leakage-controlled/prospective evaluation must remain separate from discovery yield. Dynamic lane arbitration remains an open frontier rather than an established result.
